label: Vent battery
detail: Warm alkaline vent fluid meets acidic ocean across thin iron-sulfur walls: a free ~200 mV battery.

label: Contact chemistry
detail: Reacts only to molecules that bump into its walls.

label: Diffusion
detail: Molecules wander. Crossing 1 µm takes ~0.5 ms; crossing 1 mm takes ~8 minutes.

label: Self-feeding chemistry
detail: Carbon fixation inside mineral pores, ~100 reactions per second per protocell.

label: Chemical levels
detail: About 100 bits of short-lived state per protocell.

label: Self-copying
detail: Whatever copies itself best persists.

label: RNA templates
detail: Ribozymes stuck to mineral surfaces: about 20,000 unique bits on the whole planet.

label: Pore clusters
detail: Thousands of mineral micro-compartments share one vent.

label: Ribosome
detail: A tape reader: reads three-letter codons and builds 15–20 amino acids per second.

label: Genetic code
detail: One codon table for all life, with proofreading that catches most copying errors.

label: DNA genome
detail: LUCA carried ~2.5 million DNA letters coding ~2,600 proteins, copied with about one error per billion.

label: Gene swapping
detail: Microbial mats share genes sideways between cells.

label: Early photosynthesis
detail: Sunlight harvested with sulfur and iron, no oxygen released. Planet power: 0.44 TW.

label: Smell + swim
detail: Chemical sensors read the water; a spinning flagellum runs and tumbles.

label: Four-second memory
detail: Receptor tags compare the present with about 4 seconds ago.

label: Swim toward food
detail: Tumble less when things are getting better.

label: Partner microbes
detail: Different species trade waste for food.

label: Oxygen photosynthesis
detail: Splits water with sunlight and releases oxygen.

label: 24-hour clock
detail: A three-protein clock anticipates dawn. The planning horizon grows from 4 seconds to 24 hours.

label: Quorum sensing
detail: Microbial mats vote by chemical signal across up to ~10¹⁰ cells.

label: Breathing oxygen
detail: Burning sugar with oxygen yields 30–36 ATP instead of 2. Planet power: 3.5 TW.

label: Mitochondria
detail: An engulfed bacterium becomes a power plant: ~10,000× more energy per gene.

label: Complex-cell signaling
detail: Signal cascades and an internal skeleton, ~100,000 operations per second per cell.

label: Packed chromosomes
detail: DNA wound on protein spools lets genomes grow large.

label: Cells inside cells
detail: Two cells become one.

label: Chloroplast
detail: A swallowed cyanobacterium becomes a built-in solar panel.

label: Eyespot
detail: A light-sensitive spot steers two flagella within milliseconds.

label: Sex
detail: Shuffling two genomes lets good mutations combine and bad ones get purged.

label: Many-celled bodies
detail: Clones stick together and split the work.

label: Synapse parts (spare)
detail: Proteins later used in synapses already exist, used for gluing cells together.

label: Fungal networks
detail: Fungal threads and colonial rosettes.

label: Chemical tissue waves
detail: Sponges coordinate pumping with nitric oxide and glutamate.

label: Bioelectric tissue
detail: Six cell types coordinate with peptides and voltage, with no synapses.

label: A front end
detail: Sensors cluster at the front of a two-sided body.

label: Bare nerve fibers
detail: Signals travel ~1 m/s; speed grows only with the square root of fiber width.

label: Neurons
detail: Nerve nets switch on: 10²⁰ synaptic events per second, planet-wide.

label: Firing patterns
detail: Spikes hold state for milliseconds to seconds.

label: Steering
detail: Approach good, avoid bad, in three dimensions. The first of five great brain breakthroughs.

label: Compound eyes
detail: Anomalocaris had more than 16,000 lenses per eye.

label: Three-part brain
detail: Early arthropods already had a fore-, mid- and hindbrain with layered visual centers.

label: Learning from reward
detail: Dopamine signals surprise, so the brain learns from trial and error. Breakthrough two.

label: Synaptic memory
detail: Lessons from one lifetime get written into synapse strengths (~4.7 bits each).

label: Fish schools
detail: Jawless fish move as one.

label: Myelin
detail: Insulated fibers carry signals 50–100 m/s, at ~1% of the energy per centimeter.

label: Land plants
detail: Photosynthesis moves onto the continents, and wood appears.

label: Wood-wide web
detail: Fungi link plant roots across whole forests.

label: Eyes in air
detail: Out of water, sight range grows ~100× and visible volume ~1,000,000×.

label: Look-ahead planning
detail: Prey seen minutes away rewards weighing future paths.

label: Oxygen-rich air
detail: Oxygen near 33% fuels giant flying insects.

label: Warm blood
detail: A 37 °C body keeps the brain fast, even at night.

label: Six-layer cortex
detail: The mammal cortex forms, wired to the hippocampus.

label: Mental maps
detail: Place cells hold where-am-I.

label: Imagining
detail: Replay rehearses paths not yet taken. Breakthrough three.

label: Three-bone ear
detail: Old jaw bones become ear bones for high-pitched hearing.

label: Flight controller
detail: A bigger cerebellum and pallium steer in three dimensions.

label: Insect superorganisms
detail: Ants, bees and termites coordinate ~1,000,000 workers by scent and dance.

label: Echolocation
detail: Toothed whales see with sound.

label: Dense bird brains
detail: Songbirds pack ~240 million neurons per gram.

label: Reading minds
detail: A prefrontal cortex models what others know. Breakthrough four.

label: Tool-using hands
detail: Striking stone extends what hands can do.

label: Stone tools
detail: The first memory outside a body: a knapped stone keeps a plan for 10,000+ years at zero watts.

label: Fire and cooking
detail: Cooking digests food outside the body, freeing energy for a bigger brain.

label: Engraved symbols
detail: Ochre plaques and shell beads carry meaning.

label: Speech
detail: About 39 bits per second, across all 17 languages measured.

label: Language
detail: Nested grammar moves plans and stories between minds. Breakthrough five.

label: Cave art and tallies
detail: Painted walls, notched bones and songlines.

label: Tribes
detail: Groups of ~1,500 bound by a shared language.

label: Farming
detail: Crops and herds turn sunlight into a dependable surplus.

label: Villages
detail: Settled villages of 500–2,000 people.

label: Clay writing
detail: Baked clay tablets last thousands of years with no power.

label: City-states
detail: Uruk: ~50,000 people coordinated by written ledgers.

label: Alphabet
detail: About 22 letters replace thousands of signs (~5 bits per letter).

label: Gear computer
detail: The Antikythera mechanism predicts the sky with bronze gears.

label: Empires
detail: Rome and Han China each govern ~60 million people.

label: The book
detail: Pages replace scrolls: jump straight to any passage.

label: Printing press
detail: Copying cost falls ~300×; ~20 million books in 50 years.

label: Mechanical calculators
detail: Pascal and Leibniz build adding machines.

label: Scientific journals
detail: Peer review turns science into a shared, self-correcting memory.

label: Coal and steam
detail: Technology's power use reaches 1.5 TW.

label: Telegraph
detail: Signals cross continents at ~70% of light speed, two million times faster than a nerve.

label: Punch-card machines
detail: Hollerith's machines count the 1890 US census.

label: Electronic computers
detail: ENIAC and EDVAC: ~100,000 operations per second worldwide.

label: Stored programs
detail: Instructions live in memory as data, so machines can be reprogrammed.

label: Microchips
detail: Many transistors on one silicon chip; Moore's law begins.

label: Electronic memory
detail: Magnetic cores, then DRAM, hold a running program's state.

label: ARPANET
detail: Computers start talking to each other in packets.

label: Fiber optics
detail: Light in glass carries the web.

label: Digital storage
detail: Digital storage passes all paper, film and vinyl combined.

label: World Wide Web
detail: 6.1 billion people and about a billion processors.

label: GPUs that learn
detail: Graphics chips get repurposed to train neural networks.

label: Transformers
detail: One AI architecture for language, code and proteins.

label: 84.5 TW
detail: Life uses 65 TW; technology adds 19.5 TW.

label: AI supercomputers
detail: One cluster runs 3×10²⁰ operations per second.

label: Memory everywhere
detail: Refreshed every 64 ms; refreshing alone uses ~11 GW worldwide.

label: Machines that deliberate
detail: Models think step by step before answering.

label: 15 zettabytes
detail: 1.2×10²³ bits stored, kept alive by ~20 GW of power.

label: Planetary network
detail: 8.1 billion people and 6.5 billion devices.
